holidays.name: National Eggs Benedict Day
holidays.description: Brunch gets fancy today. Poached eggs, Canadian bacon and a toasted English muffin get a blanket of silky hollandaise. Order it, make it, or just argue about whether your hollandaise is too lemony.
holidays.origin: The dish is tied to 1890s New York. The best-known story credits Lemuel Benedict, a Wall Street broker. In 1894 he supposedly ordered toast, bacon, poached eggs and hollandaise at the Waldorf Hotel to cure a hangover. This day is an unofficial food observance.
holidays.funFact: Delmonico's restaurant in New York also claims it invented the dish. Nobody has ever settled which of the two came first.

holidays.name: National Wear Your Pajamas to Work Day
holidays.description: Today you can trade the business casual for flannel, fuzzy slippers and maybe a sleep mask pushed up on your forehead. Remote workers get a head start, and office workers can try to talk their boss into it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, fun-first observance of unclear origin. It celebrates comfort and the idea that productivity doesn't have to come with a stiff collar.
holidays.funFact: The word 'pajamas' comes from the Hindi and Urdu 'pae jama', meaning 'leg garment'. British colonists brought the loose trousers home from South Asia, and they became bedtime wear in the West.

holidays.name: National Bean Counter Day
holidays.description: This day salutes the accountants, bookkeepers and number crunchers who keep the money straight. They are the people who always know where the budget went.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's a playful nod to the nickname 'bean counter', which is used for detail-obsessed finance professionals.
holidays.funFact: People have used beans for counting since ancient times. Tokens made of clay and seeds were among the earliest accounting tools.
